headline: High: dexter’s broad network egress can leak sensitive financial context, while the pair also has a default output-to-input cascade risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection between dexter and spring-integration-samples is not provable. However, dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution, so if outputs are manually bridged into the other agent, injection becomes plausible. spring-integration-samples exposes no input surface here, so the pathway is weak.
conditions: IF an operator copies dexter scratchpad content into spring-integration-samples inputs
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of model outputs into prompts
Add a human review step before reusing any generated text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter has broad network egress and calls multiple external APIs, while spring-integration-samples has no network egress. The pair can still leak financial or market data if dexter processes shared files or prompts containing sensitive data and transmits them outward. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF financial or market data is placed into dexter prompts or scratchpad files
IF dexter sends those contents to any external API during execution
mitigations: Do not place sensitive data in dexter inputs
Use redacted or synthetic datasets
Restrict dexter API keys to non-sensitive test accounts
Review outbound requests before enabling live runs
requires-engineering: isolate dexter behind an egress proxy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, but spring-integration-samples shows no write or concurrency surface. With no shared writable resource documented, a direct capability conflict is not established. If both are pointed at the same directory or mutable resource, conflicts could occur, but that is not the default shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same filesystem path
IF a shared mutable resource is introduced without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Use file locks for any shared artifact
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter can generate autonomous research outputs from external APIs, and spring-integration-samples may consume those outputs if an operator wires them together. Because no verification step is documented, B could treat A’s generated facts as authoritative and propagate errors. The pairwise cascade is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is fed dexter-generated text as authoritative input
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require source checking before reuse
Add a validation checklist for generated claims
Keep dexter outputs advisory only
Separate generation from execution roles
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on handoff

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress to third-party APIs, creating a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated or residency-bound data is processed. spring-integration-samples shows no data classes or residency controls, so it is not the primary compliance driver. Because the pairwise residency and retention posture is undocumented, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through dexter
IF any residency- or retention-bound data is sent to dexter APIs
mitigations: Use non-regulated sample data
Confirm vendor DPAs before live use
Minimize retention in upstream services
Document data flow boundaries
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
